messages:
ying (eng-ml): Heads up — after enabling FP8 kernels on H100/L40S in staging I'm seeing a mixed bag: throughput down ~8-15% on long-context runs, occasional OOMs, and a few NaNs in the attention. Root changes: transformer_engine fp8=true, kernel selector switched to fp8_matmul_opt, calibration done with per_tensor stats. Posting configs + lightweight profile.

sofia (runtime): Can you paste the TE config and full driver/CUDA/torch/transformer-engine versions?

ying (eng-ml):
```
transformer_engine:
  enabled: true
  fp8: true
  fp8_mode: 'e4m3'  # e4m3 vs e5m2
  force_kernel: 'auto'
  calibration:
    mode: 'per_tensor'
    samples: 1024
  stochastic_rounding: false
```
CUDA: 12.2
Driver: 535.113
PyTorch: 2.2.0
Transformer-Engine: 1.5.0
HW: H100 (driver machine) and L40S (some nodes)

perf-bot: Profile summary (microbench representative batch=4, seq=4096):
```
p50_latency: 142ms -> 159ms (+12%)
p99_latency: 370ms -> 480ms (+30%)
throughput_tokens/s: 78k -> 67k (-14%)
memory_peak: +8% (KV cache + quant buffers)
note: 3 samples showed softmax NaN after layer 18
```

alex (perf): Two quick hypotheses: (1) kernel selector is choosing an fp8 path optimized for small sequence lengths; for long contexts it falls back to a slower fp16 kernel in some layers causing variability. (2) KV cache handling: when fp8 is enabled we allocate extra quant scale buffers, and our prefix caching code does extra memcpy into host-visible pages -> stalls. Do an nsight/ CUPTI run and dump per-kernel times and smem usage.

sofia (runtime): +1 on CUPTI. Also try these runtime knobs:
- set batcher.max_batch_tokens to 20000 for long-context workloads
- set batcher.max_batch_items to 8
- disable continuous batching for interactive inference: batcher.continuous=false
- try transformer_engine.force_kernel='fp8_matmul_opt' and compare vs 'fp16_fallback'
- enable calibration.mode='per_channel_avg' for weights

matt (infra): Noting driver mismatch risk: L40S fleet still on driver 531.x in some racks; H100 nodes on 535.x. We've seen subtle cuBLASLt regressions across 532-535 that affect int/fp8 kernels. I'll coordinate a small driver roll to align fleets. Also verify cublasLt patch level.

ying (eng-ml): Also saw NaNs correlated with rotary embeddings and RMSNorm. Example log snippet:
```
Layer 18 attention: softmax produced NaN for batch 2, seq idx 3136
Backtrace: attention_forward -> softmax_kernel -> expf -> NaN
```
If I run same seed with fp16 fallback the NaN disappears.

sofia (runtime): That suggests numeric stability issues with fp8 accumulation or calibration scales; try: enable stochastic_rounding=true, set fp8_mode='e5m2' (more exponent bits), and increase calibration.samples to 4096. Also try running with activation scaling per_channel.

alex (perf): For kernel selection heuristics we should adjust the predictor: prefer fp16 fallback for layers where seq_len > 2048 OR batch_items > 4, and prefer fp8_opt otherwise. I can push a hotfix to the selector thresholds and add an env flag RUNTIME_FP8_SELECTOR_THRESH='{"seq":2048,"batch_items":4}'.

perf-bot: microbench A/B after selector tweak (batch=2, seq=4096):
```
A: fp8_opt (baseline fp8): tokens/s 67k, p99 480ms
B: selector-thresholded: tokens/s 73k (+9%), p99 420ms (-12%)
```

ying (eng-ml): Plan for tonight's runs:
- Run A: FP8 enabled + calibration per_channel_avg + stochastic_rounding=true + force_kernel='fp8_matmul_opt' on H100 (aligned drivers)
- Run B: FP16 fallback + KV prefetching (lockstep memcpy) + batcher tweaks (max_batch_tokens=20000)
- Collect Nsight traces, CUPTI kernel timelines, and our internal per-layer perf counters.

sofia (runtime): Also create a canary release targeting 5% production traffic and add SLA guard: if p99 latency > baseline*2 OR error_rate>0.5% then auto-fallback to fp16 pool. I'll add rollout config.

matt (infra): I'll schedule a quick driver sync for the L40S rack and post the kernel driver plan.

ying (eng-ml): Thanks all. I'll post the Nsight traces and raw CUPTI outputs in this thread when done. If anyone wants to jump on a short triage call after 18:00 UTC ping me.

sofia (runtime): Sounds good. One more ask: capture representative prompt distribution for calibration (long vs short). Calibration mismatch often causes quality regressions even when perf looks good.

ying (eng-ml): noted. Will attach sample prompts and also include failing seeds.

alex (perf): I'll draft a short perf regression test that runs nightly with fp8 enabled vs fp16 to catch drifts.

sofia (runtime): :thumbsup: keep the thread updated.
